extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: ACL OCL is a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology containing 73,285 computational linguistics papers spanning seven decades (1952–2022), with structured full texts, metadata, citation graphs, 210K figures, and links to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Crawlers were designed to fetch all PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website. PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Full-text extraction was performed using GROBID. The dataset undergoes annual updates by monitoring changes in URLs to identify new additions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, comprising 73,285 conference, journal, and workshop papers in the CL domain.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The OCL corpus focuses exclusively on peer-reviewed, open-access CL papers from ACL Anthology, which may not represent the full breadth of computational linguistics research, potentially missing lower-quality or non-peer-reviewed work.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus is limited to ACL Anthology sources only, uses open-source PDF2text (GROBID) which may yield lower quality than paid services, lacks annotations/labels for specific tasks, and does not include arXiv CL papers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables temporal topic trend analysis in computational linguistics, highlighting emerging topics like 'Ethics of NLP' and declining underrepresented topics like 'Discourse and Pragmatics' and 'Phonology, Morphology and Word Segmentation', calling for more attention to these areas.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for open research in computational linguistics, supporting tasks such as temporal topic trend analysis, metadata analysis, bibliographic research, textual analysis, citation network analysis, document layout research, and multi-modal research. It can also be used for training and fine-tuning with LLM-generated silver labels.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be updated annually to stay current with ACL Anthology data. The long-term plan is to provide full-text and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Annual updates are performed by downloading and processing papers recently added to the ACL Anthology, identifying new additions by monitoring changes in URLs. Automatically detected fields such as language and topic are added to enable further analysis.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed. Full-text extraction from PDFs was performed using GROBID, following the S2ORC-JSON format. Language detection was applied using a public toolkit with title and abstract as inputs. The dataset is provided in CSV and Apache Parquet formats.

name.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.

description.evidence: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022. The OCL further provides higher-quality structured full texts for all papers... The ACL OCL spans seven decades, containing 73K papers, alongside 210K figures.

creator.evidence: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan — College of Information Sciences and Technology, Pennsylvania State University; School of Computing, National University of Singapore

inLanguage.evidence: The ACL Anthology is an important resource that digitally archives all scientific papers in the CL domain

isLiveDataset.evidence: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website... We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages... The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. For these updates, we identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We then obtain 73,285 conference journal and workshop papers in the CL domain... the ACL Anthology only provides PDF files, which we can use to extract full texts for OCL.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC (Lo et al., 2020), since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers... it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology... only open-source toolkits are considered, although it is acknowledged that some paid PDF2text services might yield higher-quality full texts... The OCL corpus is an unlabeled resource, lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: By analyzing the topics' popularity, we ask for more attention on the emerging new topics such as 'Ethics of NLP' and the declining underrepresented topics like 'Discourse and Pragmatics' and 'Phonology, Morphology and Word Segmentation'.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The structured full texts, enriched metadata from Semantic Scholar Academic Graph, and figures provided by OCL can benefit existing research tasks as well as enable more opportunities... open scholarly datasets not only facilitate researchers in refining their task-specific data but also aid in analyzing the characteristics of scientific papers.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive. The ultimate solution is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, thus hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. For these updates, we identify new additions by monitoring changes in URLs... We add automatically detected fields such as language and topic to enable further analysis.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages... we use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files... We take the S2ORC-JSON format... To detect the language in which a document is written, we utilize a public language detection toolkit with its title and abstract as inputs... we provide our dataset in Apache Parquet, an open-source, column-oriented data format, to facilitate efficient downstream processing.
